rows.comment: Diagnostic message for telemetry, not shown in the UI.
lineComments: Log message start with work time.
Log message end with build, raster and total spans.
Telemetry key=value fields for work and build time.
Telemetry key=value fields for raster and total time.

rows.comment: Undefined MET, em dash, and a trailing 'for an activity that carries no MET' clause. State the formula and the fallback in two sentences.
lineComments: Formula with an em dash; MET is not defined.
Fallback case is wordy; 'carries' is filler.
rows.replacement:
'Calories use the activity MET (metabolic equivalent) value × your weight, adjusted by heart rate. '
'Activities with no MET value use heart rate alone.'

rows.comment: The 'not one measured on you' tail rebuts a claim nobody made, and the em dash is a tell. The estimate from age is the fact.
lineComments: Em dash and a negation that adds nothing.
rows.replacement:
'Zone edges are percentages of a maximum heart rate '
'estimated from your age.'

rows.comment: 'Both measured on you' repeats the sentence before it, and 'the gap' is vague. Name the two endpoints.
lineComments: Describes the lower endpoint, resting heart rate.
Describes the upper endpoint with its value.
Repeats what the first line already says.
rows.replacement:
'Zone edges are set between your measured resting heart rate '
'and the highest heart rate recorded for you (${maxHr.round()} bpm).'

rows.comment: Em dash and 'measured, not estimated' contrast nobody asked for. 'We have seen' is cute.
lineComments: States the basis, but 'we have seen' is vague.
Em dash and a stacked not-X contrast.
rows.replacement:
'Zone edges are percentages of the highest heart rate recorded for you '
'(${maxHr.round()} bpm).'

rows.comment: 'What this is made of' leaves 'this' undefined. Name the subject.
Awkward subject ('Nothing recorded says'). Say that no record explains the missing strain.
rows.replacement: 'No record explains why this day has no strain.'

rows.comment: Passive and wordy. Say the minutes behind the number are not stored.
lineComments: States the strain value; 'The day strain' is clumsy.
Passive: 'it was built from are not stored'.
rows.replacement:
'Day strain is ${s.toStringAsFixed(1)}. '
'This day has no stored waking minutes to chart.'

rows.comment: Direct instruction the reader can act on.
'Banked', the em dash and capitalised 'STEEP' are flourish. The useful fact is that the curve can fall later in the day.
lineComments: 'Banked' is a metaphor; em dash follows.
Explains the curve can ease; wordy.
'STEEP parts already happened' is rhetorical emphasis.
Keeps the real fact: minute count.
rows.replacement:
'Effort above your usual waking pace. The line can fall later in the day '
'if intensity returns to that pace. '
'Built from $drawn recorded waking minutes.'

rows.comment: 'Saw' is cute; the band records data.
Loose passive and a stacked clause. Say that strain sums recorded minutes and tell the reader what to avoid.
lineComments: 'reads lower' is soft; says the same thing as line 3.
rows.replacement:
'Strain sums the recorded minutes, so a partly worn day scores '
'lower than a fully worn day. '
'Do not compare the two.'

rows.comment: 'These' is undefined; the section explains how strain is calculated.
TRIMP is undefined jargon. Keep the algorithm name and the 0–21 range, and define the term.
rows.replacement: 'Banister TRIMP (training impulse) over your waking heart rate, scaled to 0–21.'

rows.comment: Passive 'was integrated against', em dash, and 'not measured' rebuttal. State the assumed maximum and its source.
lineComments: Em dash; gives the estimate source.
rows.replacement:
'Strain uses an assumed maximum heart rate of '
'${max.round()} bpm, estimated from your age and your strap.'

rows.comment: Semicolon and stacked contrasts. Say what the zone bar uses and why strain keeps the assumed maximum.
lineComments: 'Measured ceiling instead' is a contrast with a vague noun.
Passive 'has not been moved onto it'.
Reason is good but 'rewrite every score you have ever seen' is hyperbole.
rows.replacement:
'The zone bar above uses the highest heart rate recorded for you. '
'Strain keeps the assumed maximum, because changing it '
'would alter every past strain score.'

rows.comment: 'Anchor' is jargon. Name the input and the consequence of a missing night.
rows.replacement:
'The other input is your resting heart rate from the night before. '
'If the band missed that night, the strain for the whole day shifts.'
